items.title: Cisco UCS and UCS-Based Appliances UEFI Shell Secure Boot Bypass Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A UEFI Shell vulnerability in Cisco UCS servers allows Secure Boot bypass via memory write commands.
items.summary: A vulnerability in the UEFI Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances allows authenticated or physical attackers to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks. The flaw stems from memory write commands remaining accessible in the UEFI Shell while Secure Boot is enabled. An attacker can select the UEFI Shell at boot time to modify UEFI memory variables, manipulate the preboot environment, and execute unauthorized software. Cisco has released software updates to address the issue with no available workarounds.
key_facts: Affected products: Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances
items.bottom_line: Administrators must update Cisco UCS firmware to patch a UEFI Shell vulnerability that permits Secure Boot bypass and unauthorized code execution.

claims.text: A vulnerability in the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Shell implementation of Cisco UCS Servers and UCS-based appliances could allow an authenticated attacker with valid credentials for a user account with the role of user or admin or an unauthenticated attacker with physical access to an affected device to bypass UEFI Secure Boot validation checks and execute unauthorized software.

items.title: CVE-2026-78355 (HIGH 8.7): A path traversal vulnerability in the OTRS SendSupportBundle functionality allows an authenticated administra…
items.one_liner: Authenticate as an admin on vulnerable OTRS installations and you can trigger path traversal to delete files outside the intended directory.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-78355, a high-severity path traversal vulnerability in OTRS, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw exists in the OTRS SendSupportBundle functionality and allows an authenticated administrator to reference file paths outside the intended directory, potentially leading to the deletion of files accessible by the OTRS application process. The issue affects OTRS versions 7.0.X, 8.0.X, 2023.X, 2024.X, 2025.X, and 2026.X before 2026.7.X, as well as ((OTRS)) Community Edition 6.x and prior. Exploitation requires valid administrative access, and direct arbitrary file disclosure to attackers has not been demonstrated.

items.title: Zero-click spyware infecting devices through online ads, researchers say
items.one_liner: Discover-Tech and Candiru deployed zero-click spyware via online ads to compromise targets across high-security government and international networks.
items.summary: Researchers from Citizen Lab and Confiant uncovered a global zero-click spyware campaign where Israel-based ad tech firm Discover-Tech used malicious digital ads to infect target devices. Operating through its Controlium platform, Discover-Tech collaborated with blacklisted mercenary spyware company Candiru to automatically execute JavaScript and compromise devices the moment an ad was rendered. The campaign targeted at least 45 Al Jazeera journalists and served ads onto national-security-sensitive networks globally, including NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, Estonia's RIA, the IAEA, and the International Criminal Court. Major ad platforms such as Google have since blocked Discover-Tech after analyzing billions of ad placement records.
key_facts: Affected journalists: At least 45 at Al Jazeera
Targeted networks: NATO, U.S. Department of Defense, Estonia RIA, IAEA, International Criminal Court
Ad records analyzed: 4 billion records over 4 months
items.bottom_line: Ad networks can be weaponized to deliver zero-click spyware via malicious JavaScript execution the moment an advertisement is rendered.

items.title: Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks
items.one_liner: The Hirudo Android banking trojan replaces legitimate banking apps with custom-patched versions to bypass built-in security checks.
items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a new Android banking trojan named Hirudo that replaces legitimate banking applications with patched versions to bypass in-app security checks. The malware targets credentials and facilitates device takeover, screen capture, and SMS theft across multiple countries including Indonesia, India, and China. Dropper apps utilize functional WebViews as lures while executing scripts to verify if the Hirudo payload is installed and leveraging a non-functional VPN connection to evade cloud-based checks. The custom-built application replacements embed hooking engines designed to blind signature, accessibility, screen-capture, and Play Integrity checks.
key_facts: Targeted regions: Indonesia, China, India, Mexico, Morocco, Thailand
Dropper apps: Shopora, 1V1 X, KoiShort, ZoyaTV
items.bottom_line: Banking malware is evolving past permission manipulation to directly patch and blind security controls inside target Android applications.

items.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
items.one_liner: Critical zero-day chain actively exploited in Ivanti VPN appliances requires immediate patching and thorough forensic auditing.
items.summary: An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances to execute commands as root without authentication, as reported by Volexity on October 13. The attack chain consists of an authentication bypass and remote code execution flaw tracked as CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS 8.6) alongside a privilege escalation vulnerability. While patches are available for two of the flaws, a fix for the privilege escalation is still pending. The threat actor, tracked as UTA0576, used the exploit chain to harvest credentials and conduct password-spraying attacks.
key_facts: Affected Version: Connect Secure before version 25.1.3.0
items.bottom_line: Ivanti Connect Secure appliances face active zero-day exploitation enabling unauthenticated root access, and standard integrity checks fail to detect the memory-resident compromise.

items.one_liner: Hugging Face's LFM2.5-24B-A2B brings fast, on-device agent reasoning and tool-use capabilities to edge hardware.
items.summary: Hugging Face has introduced LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a new mixture-of-experts model optimized for on-device agentic tasks and tool use. items.title: CVE-2026-104798 - My Calendar <= 3.8.7 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to 'mcs' Parameter via Reflected Shortcode Injection into 'above' Attribute
items.one_liner: A critical privilege escalation flaw in a popular WordPress plugin lets unauthenticated attackers take over the main admin account via shortcode injection.
items.summary: The My Calendar plugin for WordPress up to version 3.8.7 is vulnerable to an unauthenticated privilege escalation via reflected shortcode injection into the 'above' attribute. The public 'mcs' GET parameter is reflected unsanitized into post content and processed by `do_shortcode`, allowing unauthenticated attackers to invoke arbitrary PHP functions. This enables a call chain that passes the shortcode parameters to `edit_user()`, coercing the user ID to 1 and overwriting the initial Administrator account credentials to grant full wp-admin access.
key_facts: Product: My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress
Vulnerability: Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Reflected Shortcode Injection
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve full WordPress admin takeover by exploiting unsanitized GET parameters in My Calendar versions 3.8.7 and below.

claims.text: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.7.
claims.support_span: The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.7.

claims.text: This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to invoke arbitrary loaded PHP functions, enabling a call chain in which the shortcode `$params` array is passed to `edit_user()` — which PHP coerces to integer `1` as the `$user_id` argument — overwriting the credentials of the initial Administrator account (user ID 1) and granting the attacker full wp-admin access.

items.one_liner: Audit and restrict PAN-OS management interfaces to internal IP addresses or jump boxes to mitigate CVE-2026-0322.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks disclosed CVE-2026-0322, an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the management interface of PAN-OS software affecting PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. items.title: CVE-2026-103903 (HIGH 8.7): An incorrect authorization vulnerability in the WinBox authentication flow of MikroTik RouterOS allows a remo…
items.one_liner: A MikroTik RouterOS WinBox authentication flaw lets low-privilege users acquire full administrator sessions.
items.summary: An incorrect authorization vulnerability in the WinBox authentication flow of MikroTik RouterOS allows a remote authenticated attacker with low-privilege WinBox access to hijack the policy of a higher-privilege account. By verifying the stage-one EC-SRP challenge using their own credentials and supplying a target username in stage two, an attacker can obtain a full administrative session without knowing the password. This session can subsequently be used to escalate the privileges of the attacker's own account. CVSS base score is 8.7.

items.title: CVE-2026-103895 - miniOrange OTP Login, Verification and SMS Notifications <= 5.5.8 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Delay OTP Grace State
items.one_liner: WordPress sites running vulnerable miniOrange OTP Login plugins can be completely taken over by unauthenticated attackers exploiting flawed Delay OTP grace state logic.
items.summary: The miniOrange OTP Login, Verification and SMS Notifications plugin for WordPress up to version 5.5.8 is vulnerable to an unauthenticated authentication bypass via the `mo_by_pass_login()` function. The flaw occurs because `mo_delay_otp_process()` short-circuits the authentication flow before password validation or the administrator intent gate can execute, and the Delay OTP grace flag is stored as a `user_meta` row keyed solely by target user ID without session or device binding. Unauthenticated attackers can leverage this by supplying a known username with the `mo_wp_login_intent=otp` parameter and any non-empty password to inherit a legitimate user's active grace window. Successful exploitation requires the site to have OTP-only login and Delay OTP Verification enabled, with the target account currently within its configured interval.

items.one_liner: An eval-injection flaw in unmaintained VestaControlPanel <= 0.9.8-26 permits authenticated users to achieve root RCE.
items.summary: A critical tenant-to-host escalation vulnerability (VESTACP-2026-001 / CVE-equivalent) exists in Vesta Control Panel versions 0.9.8-26 and earlier. VestaCP stores object configurations as KEY='value' lines under user directories, which are subsequently parsed using the shell command `eval` within administrative scripts running with root privileges. An authenticated panel user can inject unescaped single quotes into fields such as cron commands or domains, leading to arbitrary OS command execution as root the next time the objects are parsed. Because VestaCP has been unmaintained upstream since September 2019, no official vendor fix exists, posing ongoing risks for deployments on legacy VPS templates.
key_facts: Weaknesses: CWE-78 (OS Command Injection), CWE-95 (Eval Injection)

Verbalized confidence proved inconsistent, yielding high expected calibration error and poor failure prediction AUROC. Implementing a transparent, workflow-aware controller successfully improved utility and reduced missed escalations across all models, though a lexical stress test revealed that simple rule detectors failed entirely on unseen paraphrases.
items.bottom_line: Healthcare LLM agents frequently fail to escalate critical workflow exceptions under uncertainty unless governed by dedicated workflow-aware controllers.

items.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments

Furthermore, training on a mocked train-ticketing app successfully transferred to a physical phone, boosting real-world task success from 28.8% to 48.1%.

items.title: Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents
items.one_liner: Evaluate and audit self-improving agent architectures against post-deployment skill drift using the CODA framework.
items.summary: Self-improving AI agents that use skill-policy co-evolution suffer from a fragility trap where policy models become brittle when operating on drifted skill banks after deployment. The shared cooperative acceptance rule ties agent competence tightly to the specific training bank, making performance highly sensitive to post-deployment edits like rewriting, adding, or removing skills. To address this blind spot, researchers introduced the CO-evolution Drift Audit (CODA), a deployment-oriented evaluation protocol that measures consistency under edits and resistance to corrupted skills. Across multiple tested methods, worst-case success dropped 5-13 points below peak performance, erasing over half of the gains over baseline models.
items.bottom_line: Co-evolved AI agents experience catastrophic performance drops when their underlying skill banks drift post-deployment, exposing a critical evaluation blind spot.

items.title: Thinking in Graphs: Neo4j-Backed Exploit-Chain Reasoning for LLM Penetration-Testing Agents
items.one_liner: ChainGraph externalizes exploit-chain reasoning into a Neo4j graph for LLM pen-testing agents, turning isolated findings into attack paths.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ChainGraph, a pattern that integrates Neo4j property graphs with LLM penetration-testing agents via the Model Context Protocol to improve exploit-chain reasoning. Traditional coding agents treat an engagement as a flat list of findings in a context window, missing how low-severity exposures can be chained into critical paths. ChainGraph stores typed nodes and pre/post-condition edges in Neo4j while formalizing operator queries for next-step inference, pathing, and severity promotion. Tested on a synthetic Active Directory engagement, the approach successfully promoted three Medium findings to Critical when their path to the forest root was materialized, while cutting the reasoning payload token proxy by approximately 98%.
items.bottom_line: Externalizing exploit-chain reasoning into a property graph prevents LLM pen-testing agents from missing critical attack paths hidden in flat context windows.

items.title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
items.one_liner: ASU provides a secure cryptographic gateway for AI agent approvals, addressing critical flaws where approvals can be bypassed or manipulated after authorization.
items.summary: AI agents frequently pause for approval before executing critical actions, but existing approval workflows lack effect binding and verification. Testing twelve approval attacks against frameworks like AP2, Microsoft's action-bound approval design, and MCP elicitation revealed widespread vulnerabilities, including missing third-party verifiable records and post-approval argument changes. To resolve this, researchers developed ASU (Agent Step-Up), a gateway that generates a trusted approval card from a canonical effect descriptor and uses a smartphone passkey to sign its cryptographic digest. Formal verification and extensive trials demonstrate that ASU successfully stops substitution, replay, grant stretching, and significantly reduces forged-narration attacks.

items.bottom_line: Current AI agent approval mechanisms are vulnerable to post-approval argument changes and spoofing, but passkey-backed canonical effect binding can securely mitigate these risks.

items.title: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
items.one_liner: INFUSE benchmark evaluates indirect prompt injection across long-horizon agentic workflows, revealing vulnerability across major LLMs.
items.summary: Researchers introduced INFUSE, an end-to-end benchmark designed to evaluate indirect prompt injection (IPI) across long-horizon agentic workflows involving shell commands, code modifications, and remote services. INFUSE features 40 realistic tasks and a structured taxonomy of 56 attack scenarios across five threat categories, testing attacks injected through realistic interaction surfaces rather than isolated prompts. Evaluating 19 LLMs from major families produced over 41,000 adversarial trajectories, revealing a mean attack success rate of 19.6% under LLM evaluation and 15.4% under heuristics, with per-model rates reaching up to 41.9%. The study found that while guard models provide limited protection, prompt-level instructional hardening successfully reduced mean attack success from 58.2% to 14.3% with trade-offs.
items.bottom_line: Long-horizon agentic workflows are highly susceptible to indirect prompt injection across realistic interaction surfaces, though prompt hardening reduces success rates.

items.title: MSP: Modality Self-Play for Training Multimodal LLMs Without Paired Cross-Modal Data
items.one_liner: MSP is a new training framework that enables multimodal LLMs to compose unseen modalities using text proxies without paired cross-modal data.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Modality Self-Play (MSP), a training framework designed to build multimodal foundation models without requiring paired cross-modal datasets. By using anchor-supporting proxy textual descriptions of unseen modalities, the framework acts as a semantic bridge between observed data modalities like images or audio. This approach enables zero-shot modality composition, allowing models to integrate and reason over multiple unseen non-text modalities at inference time. Empirically, MSP achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks while eliminating the need for expensive paired cross-modal supervision.

items.title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation
items.one_liner: Advanced LLM judges are increasingly blind to runtime stack tampering, accepting malicious modifications that preserve standard output behaviors.
items.summary: LLM-agent evaluation frameworks typically report behavioral scores while failing to track the underlying runtime stack, creating a vulnerability known as deployment-integrity blindness where tampered deployments can pass output-only evaluations. The authors introduce DIB-Bench to measure this across 7,560 examples and six tamper types, revealing that stronger evaluators accept more tampered outputs, with mean acceptance rising from 88.6% for rule-based scorers to 94.1% for GPT-5-nano. To address this, the paper demonstrates that a manifest-hash identity channel can detect zero-output-shift tampers with zero samples, and proposes a graded deployment-identity descriptor for evaluation reports.
items.bottom_line: Stronger LLM evaluators fail to catch tampered agent runtimes, making manifest-hash identity verification necessary for deployment integrity.

items.title: MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair
items.one_liner: MemScope introduces fine-grained, evidence-grounded code patching to safely evolve agent memory architectures without broad rewrites.
items.summary: MemScope is an evidence-grounded framework designed for localized, in-place evolution of LLM agent memory architectures using execution feedback. Unlike coarse-grained scoring approaches that lead to large-scale code rewrites, MemScope's tool-using Patch Agent jointly inspects raw execution traces, runtime memory states, and current code to precisely locate failures and apply bounded edits under specific safety constraints. Across multiple benchmarks including GAIA, xBench, and ALFWorld, MemScope significantly improves task success rates while introducing minimal code-change ratios, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine-grained execution evidence for architecture repair.
items.bottom_line: AI agent memory architectures can be effectively and safely repaired using fine-grained execution trace inspection and localized code patching.

items.title: What Survives Self-Evolution: Provenance Marks in Copied Agent Harnesses
items.one_liner: Standard provenance watermarks fail against LLM self-evolution rewriting attacks, necessitating robust table-based tracking methods.
items.summary: Agent harnesses often leak, allowing plagiarists to pass them through automated self-evolvers to claim the code as their own under covert rewriting attacks. Evaluating provenance mark survival under this attack shows that published marks fail completely—KGW in prompts survives zero out of 12 copies, while AgentMark survives in five out of 12. A new provenance scheme based on the ordered near-tied entries of an object-location table survives baseline rewrites and can be detected in 62 of 76 copies, though scheme-aware plagiarists or general code requests can successfully remove the key in most cases.
items.bottom_line: Existing prompt watermarks fail to survive automated LLM harness rewriting, though structured table-based provenance marks show higher resilience.

items.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
items.one_liner: RealtimeBench and TORSI tackle the latency bottleneck of LLM agents by training fast student models on insights from slow teachers in live environments.
items.summary: Evaluating LLM agents in static environments fails to capture performance under real-world time constraints where environments change during inference. To address this, researchers introduced RealtimeBench, comprising 180 tasks across six game types where games run continuously during execution. Paired evaluations demonstrate that slower, highly accurate models lose their advantage when the clock keeps ticking. To improve real-time performance, the authors propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI), an approach where a slow teacher model analyzes failures in paused games to write reusable instructions for a fast student model, raising average test scores across models.
items.bottom_line: LLM agent effectiveness degrades under continuous time constraints, but offline recursive self-improvement frameworks can bridge the performance gap.

items.title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation
items.one_liner: IneqAgent combines LLM reasoning and symbolic backends to achieve high success rates in formal mathematical inequality proving in Lean4.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced IneqAgent, an agentic framework that combines LLM reasoning with symbolic computation backends—such as sum-of-squares, Bernstein, and successive difference-substitution—for formal inequality proving in Lean4. Coordinated via lemma-level Monte Carlo Tree Search, the system generates exact certificates and checks them against original theorem statements. Using DeepSeek-V4-Flash, IneqAgent solved 175 of 186 problems (94.09%) across four benchmarks, outperforming direct agent methods while producing Lean-verified strengthenings of mathematical conjectures.
items.bottom_line: Integrating LLM search with symbolic computation backends enables high-accuracy formal inequality proving and verification in Lean4.

items.title: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows
items.one_liner: Kolab benchmark reveals that frontier AI models struggle to effectively collaborate with human experts on long-horizon professional workflows.
items.summary: To address the gap between automated benchmark performance and real-world utility, researchers have introduced Kolab, a dataset containing over 115 hours of screen recordings of 50 professionals collaborating with agents on long-horizon workflows. Analysis reveals that effective collaborative agents must anticipate user modifications and assess workflow quality without constant feedback. Evaluations show that frontier models overestimate collaboration quality and struggle to distinguish between high- and low-quality interactions, indicating that current agents are not yet equipped for long-horizon professional collaboration.
items.bottom_line: Current frontier LLM agents fail to accurately model and understand real-world human-agent collaboration in long-horizon professional tasks.

items.title: Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research
items.one_liner: A team of autonomous Claude Opus 5.5 agents successfully post-trained a raw base model to match official instruct performance.
items.summary: Researchers built Athanor, an open agent-native system designed to test autonomous post-training research capabilities on real GPUs without external teacher models or human advice. In a 104-hour campaign, a team of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents upgraded Qwen3-4B-Base from 15.9 to 67.3 on a development suite, matching or surpassing the official Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 model. The agents achieved this through self-directed methods including SFT on public reasoning data, reinforcement learning, weight merging, and self-distillation. This demonstrates that current frontier agents possess the engineering capacity to autonomously drive core machine learning research tasks.
items.bottom_line: Frontier AI agents can autonomously execute full post-training research campaigns to build competitive generalist models.

items.title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming
items.one_liner: Screwtape demonstrates a transcript-editing red-teaming pipeline that forces LLM agent monitors to miss unauthorized behaviors.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Screwtape, an adversarial pipeline designed to convert real agent execution transcripts into attacks that bypass action-only monitors. By using an LLM attacker to iteratively edit transcripts until a specified harm is achieved without executing the actions directly, the pipeline tests monitor robustness against evasive behaviors. Tested against 94 Claude Code and Codex transcripts, Screwtape successfully generated 35 attacks that evaded local monitors, with six confirmed to bypass a held-out monitor from a frontier developer. This technique provides developers and evaluators with a scalable methodology to uncover blind spots in AI safety monitoring frameworks without requiring direct infrastructure access.

items.title: SkillNEO: Non-Elitist Evolutionary Optimization of Agent Skills
items.one_liner: SkillNEO uses non-elitist evolutionary optimization to let LLM agents retain and refine partial skill repairs across multi-step tasks.
items.summary: Researchers introduce SkillNEO (Non-Elitist Evolutionary Optimization for Agent Skills), a framework designed to evolve procedural agent skills without discarding useful partial repairs that temporarily drop in score. Traditional elitist methods often discard low-reward intermediate versions during multi-step edits, whereas SkillNEO separately selects execution versions and repair targets by comparing related task performances. Across 86 SkillsBench tasks in eight domains, SkillNEO raises GPT-5.4 Mini's average reward from 49.1% to 66.4% and allows weaker models to generate reusable procedural knowledge that enhances more capable agents like Luna and GPT-5.5.

items.title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
items.one_liner: ARIA introduces a runtime inspection and repair framework that intercepts and corrects errors in multi-agent LLM systems on the fly.
items.summary: Researchers introduce ARIA (Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment), a framework designed to inspect ongoing multi-agent system executions and apply verified runtime repairs before mistakes propagate. By collecting over 24,000 trajectories across multiple benchmarks and compiling the ARIA dataset containing 3,953 verified repair pairs, the authors train a compact model to recognize when intervention is necessary and how to correct live runs. The trained model demonstrates robust generalization across unseen frameworks and host models, moving correction search from post-hoc analysis into active runtime supervision.
items.bottom_line: ARIA provides a scalable method to train compact models to intercept and correct multi-agent execution errors in real time.

items.title: Probe-and-Resume: When and How to Evaluate Agent Execution
items.one_liner: Probe-and-Resume improves LLM agent evaluation by deferring critic execution to terminal states and granting it fork-access to uncover hidden environment states.
items.summary: Researchers have evaluated test-time search configurations using Monte Carlo tree search in terminal-based computer-use environments and found they fail to meaningfully improve task success due to poor intermediate state evaluation by critics. To resolve this, they introduced "Probe-and-Resume," a policy where a critic is invoked exclusively when an agent claims completion, utilizing read, write, and execute access on a state fork to uncover hidden states. Tested on Terminal-Bench 2.1, this design increased task success by 8.4 percentage points over conventional MCTS critics while operating at under half the cost of a Codex CLI agent.
items.bottom_line: Delaying critic evaluation until completion and granting it forked environment access drastically improves agent execution success while cutting operational costs.

items.title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
items.one_liner: A new test-time multi-agent aggregation framework uses bias control and injection to improve collective LLM reasoning accuracy.
items.summary: Multi-agent reasoning with LLMs often suffers from non-semantic biases such as majority pressure and response-style preferences that distort collective decision-making. The authors demonstrate that these biases can be systematically controlled to improve initial answer selection and exploited via bias injection to elicit decision instability as a reliability signal. Based on these insights, the researchers introduce a test-time aggregation framework that applies bias control through style-normalized reasoning traces and bias injection by placing selected answers in the minority. This approach achieves higher average accuracy and token efficiency across benchmarks without requiring validation data or prior model strength knowledge.
items.bottom_line: Controlling and injecting biases during multi-agent LLM aggregation significantly improves decision accuracy and provides robust reliability signals.

items.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards
items.one_liner: Agent security guards exhibit language sensitivity, with smaller and purpose-built models frequently altering safety verdicts when prompts are translated.
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether language choice impacts step-level AI guard decisions by translating user instructions across multiple languages while keeping tool calls and observations identical. In contrast, frontier models like Gemini 3.8 Flash maintained consistent verdicts regardless of input language.

items.title: From Detection to Decision: Calibration and Deferral for Prompt-Injection Detection
items.one_liner: An evaluation of prompt-injection defense classifiers shows that probabilistic confidence scores struggle under distribution shift and require excessive escalation rates.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated probabilistic prompt-injection detection models, including Jev, Llama Prompt Guard 2 classifiers, and an LLM-based judge across 47,611 held-out examples to assess their reliability under distribution shift. The study found that while the LLM judge achieved the highest overall discrimination (AUROC 0.897), native probabilistic outputs and classifier scores do not establish reliable security decisions without substantial escalation rates. Specifically, achieving a 1% false-negative rate required more than 91.8% input escalation across all evaluated gate-reviewer configurations.
items.bottom_line: Current probabilistic prompt-injection classifiers fail to provide reliable autonomous security decisions under distribution shift without incurring massive false-positive escalation rates.

items.one_liner: GitHub Security Lab's new autonomous fuzzing agent handles harness creation, AFL++ execution, and crash triage for C/C++ projects.
items.summary: GitHub Security Lab has released the Fuzzing Taskflow, an autonomous fuzzing pipeline built on the Taskflow Agent framework to automate vulnerability discovery in C/C++ projects. The tool relies on Claude Sonnet 5 by default to bypass security guardrails and handle decision-making while Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools handle execution. Because the agent executes arbitrary commands directly on the host without containerization, developers must run it exclusively inside disposable environments like GitHub Codespaces.

items.one_liner: PortSwigger's Turbo Intruder and Burp Suite now support HTTP/3, enabling high-speed fuzzing over 100,000 requests per second and advanced race condition attacks.
items.summary: PortSwigger Research has released updates adding HTTP/3 support to both Turbo Intruder and Burp Suite via the new HTTP/3 Adapter plugin. Running over Wi-Fi against remote hosts, the HTTP/3 engine can comfortably exceed 100,000 requests per second (RPS) and scale up to 180,000 RPS from cloud instances. To maximize fuzzing efficiency, operators should minimize request sizes, utilize the :authority pseudo-header, and leverage Burp Suite's AUTO engine. Additionally, the release introduces two race condition techniques: the Single Datagram Attack for mitigating TOCTOU windows and Server-Side Race Orchestration using the QPACK Blocked Streams technique.

items.title: QuasiLeak-Bench: Evaluating LLM-Based Privacy Detectors on Policy-Conditioned Quasi-Evidence Group Recovery
items.one_liner: A new benchmark, QuasiLeak-Bench, exposes how poorly current locally deployable LLM privacy detectors handle jointly revealing quasi-identifiers under specific disclosure policies.
items.summary: Researchers introduce QuasiLeak-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based privacy detectors on policy-conditioned quasi-evidence group recovery. Natural language messages often contain weak quasi-identifiers that jointly reveal private attributes, and detecting whether such exposures violate privacy depends heavily on sender-specified disclosure policies. To establish reliable ground truth, the authors built a reverse-construction pipeline that selects weak quasi-identifiers, composes them into verified quasi-evidence groups, and generates surrounding documents. Experiments reveal that existing privacy detectors transfer poorly and locally deployable LLM-based detectors lag far behind proprietary models by missing most groups altogether, though fine-tuning a 4B model significantly improves performance.

items.title: Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents
items.one_liner: Fine-tuning language agents for selective action withdrawal improves recall but introduces rule-specific regression risks.
items.summary: Tool-using language agents must dynamically revise prepared actions when evidence changes or authorization is revoked, a capability studied via supervised fine-tuning in the NAQD-Env synthetic environment. items.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation in S3-Compatible Object Storage under Client Concurrency
items.one_liner: Understand the performance and storage overhead of deploying ML-KEM in high-concurrency S3-compatible object stores.
items.summary: Researchers benchmarked the impact of post-quantum ML-KEM key encapsulation on S3-compatible object storage under heavy client concurrency using up to 500 concurrent workers. They found that per-object ML-KEM encryption reduced throughput by 4.0 to 4.9% in the main client only when the processor was at or near full load. The permanent storage footprint overhead is an additional 1,056 bytes per object compared to classical key exchange. Controlled experiments showed that the performance loss largely depends on the software library's calling conventions and client implementation details.
items.bottom_line: Transitioning cloud object stores to ML-KEM introduces a predictable 1,056-byte per-object storage penalty and minimal throughput degradation under CPU saturation.

items.title: OmicsBench: a long-horizon multi-turn benchmark of AI agents on research-study-scale bioinformatics
items.one_liner: OmicsBench evaluates AI agents on multi-turn bioinformatics research tasks, uncovering significant long-horizon reasoning and failure modes.
items.summary: Researchers introduced OmicsBench, a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on research-study-scale tasks. The benchmark features 97 tasks structured as directed acyclic graphs comprising 662 underlying subtasks, evaluated deterministically with optional in-context feedback. Testing 12 models across three harnesses revealed that agents average 3.6 hours per task and fail to saturate the benchmark, scoring between 0.43 and 0.57 without feedback and 0.54 to 0.67 with it. Furthermore, multi-turn evaluation exposed qualitative agent shortcomings, such as applying incorrect statistical filters or fabricating answers from memory on dependent subtasks.

items.title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding

Evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that DocPilot enhances frontier vision-language models while allowing a compact 4B model to compete effectively against much larger architectures.

items.title: CascadeLedger: Counterfactual Auditing of Information and Resource Integrity in LLM Cascades
items.one_liner: CascadeLedger is a counterfactual auditing framework that verifies information and resource integrity in LLM cascades.

items.title: EvolvingBrain: An Adaptive Skill System for Multi-modal Agents Self-Evolution in Open Worlds
items.one_liner: EvolvingBrain is an adaptive skill system that enables multi-modal agents to autonomously self-evolve and build skill hierarchies in open worlds.
items.summary: Researchers proposed EvolvingBrain, an adaptive skill system that serves as an architecture for multi-modal agent self-evolution in open-world environments. The system combines Stratified Skill Self-Evolution—which extracts procedural and problematic patterns to build a multi-granularity skill hierarchy—with State-Aware Adaptive Execution, which summarizes long-horizon interactions into structured memory. Experiments on VAB-Minecraft and DiscoveryWorld showed that EvolvingBrain successfully improves task success rates and generalization capabilities.

items.title: Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure
items.one_liner: Diviner is an agentic root-cause analysis system deployed at Meta that uses a human-governed reliability lifecycle for large-scale infrastructure.
items.summary: Researchers at Meta introduced Diviner (Domain-Informed Verifiable Incident Navigation through Evidence and Review), an agentic root-cause analysis system designed for large-scale distributed systems. Generic language-model agents often fail due to stale context, false assumptions, and observability overload, prompting Diviner to adopt a four-stage reliability lifecycle comprising Encode, Execute, Evaluate, and Adapt. The system utilizes scoped skills, versioned workflows, and adaptive execution combined with human-governed operational-knowledge updates to maintain evidence-linked hypotheses during incident investigations.

items.title: Who May Release an Agent's Promise? Standing over Commitments in Multi-Party Chat
items.one_liner: Multi-party AI chat assistants frequently fail to respect proper standing for canceling commitments unless equipped with a self-kept commitment ledger and release policies.
items.summary: When an AI assistant makes a promise to a user during multi-party chat, determining who holds the standing to cancel or release that commitment is critical. In a controlled multi-party chat evaluation across six models, researchers found that smaller models often wrongly obey unauthorized peers, while larger models tend to drop commitments too easily on a peer's command. While instructions alone fail to curb overrides, implementing a self-kept commitment ledger combined with a clear release policy successfully prevents unauthorized overrides in most models, significantly boosting strict execution accuracy.

items.one_liner: Matoi is an authorization framework that separates consequence evidence to enable secure, auditable reuse for agent operations.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Matoi, an authorization framework that separates reusable consequence evidence from current execution authority and durable occurrence history. items.one_liner: AiO-Mem uses process-rewarded reinforcement learning to optimize memory retrieval and writing for long-context language model agents.

items.one_liner: ExecWeave is a local-first system that links application traces with OS telemetry to provide execution provenance for AI agents.

items.title: RAC: A Relational Agent Contract for Constraint-Governed Engineering Tasks
items.one_liner: A new action contract for engineering agents separates semantic decisions from derived consequences, boosting reliability in tasks like PCB routing.
items.summary: Engineering agents often fail in constraint-governed tasks because they attempt to handle both semantic decisions and precise derived consequences like geometry or timing. items.title: AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks
items.one_liner: AlphaDiana provides a modular measurement framework for diagnosing AI agent reasoning performance, revealing that agent harnesses do not universally improve accuracy.
items.summary: AlphaDiana is a newly introduced measurement system designed to evaluate AI agents on verifiable reasoning tasks by providing modular interfaces for datasets, agents, environments, and scorers. It preserves harness-native control loops while separating file reuse and memory retention controls, enabling both macro analyses of complete agents and micro interventions on components like tools, skills, and memory. Studying multiple open-source models and harnesses across answer-based and interactive benchmarks, researchers discovered that harnesses do not consistently improve reasoning accuracy; tool gains can be negated by losses on natively solvable questions, and component interventions yield mixed results. AlphaDiana links execution status, behavior, and output token usage to traces to assist developers in diagnosing failures under matched conditions.

items.title: Rubric Judgments Lack Uncertainty: Conformal Weighting for LLM Evaluation
items.one_liner: URW uses split-conformal calibration to weight LLM rubric judgments by uncertainty, improving downstream RL alignment.
items.summary: Rubric-based evaluation of LLMs uniformly aggregates binary judgments across criteria, treating all judgments with equal certainty and ignoring individual uncertainty variations. Experiments demonstrate that URW improves pairwise preference accuracy and enhances downstream RL alignment.
items.bottom_line: Accounting for judgment uncertainty in LLM evaluations via conformal weighting prevents noisy feedback from degrading downstream reinforcement learning.

items.title: Evaluating Model Capabilities After Benchmark Saturation

items.summary: As rapid advancements in AI capabilities cause traditional benchmarks to saturate, researchers investigate whether complete execution transcripts retain valuable information for assessing model performance. items.title: Planning Commitment of LLM under Partial Observability
items.one_liner: An evaluation of LLM planning under partial observability highlights the trade-off between aggressive efficiency and conservative safety.
items.summary: Researchers investigated the planning commitment strategies of Large Language Models under partial observability, contrasting aggressive planners that commit to long plans based on unobserved state assumptions with conservative planners that restrict planning to observed data. items.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
items.one_liner: An audit of AI agent safety evaluations reveals that benchmark dataset formatting artifacts and shortcut cues heavily distort guard performance metrics.

items.title: Reliance Industries share price falls 2.5% despite Jio IPO buzz: What should Mukesh Ambani stock investors do?

items.title: MSCI Freezes Turkey Indexes as Fund Turmoil Fuels Scrutiny
items.one_liner: MSCI froze Turkish equity index changes and warned of emerging-market reclassification amid fund manipulation scrutiny.
items.summary: MSCI Inc. has frozen specific index changes for Turkish equities and stepped up market scrutiny following a fund industry crisis involving allegations of artificially inflated share prices in low-free-float stocks. FTSE Russell has similarly flagged concerns over free-float data while keeping Turkey's advanced emerging market status under review.

items.bottom_line: Turkey's equity market faces potential emerging-market reclassification by MSCI following fund manipulation scandals and sharp selloffs.

items.title: With inflation rising, will Warsh keep investors guessing?
items.one_liner: Fed Chairman Warsh's intentional silence on monetary policy and reaction functions is heightening market volatility amid rising inflation.
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is facing rising inflation pressures as producer prices recorded their largest monthly gain in over four years and consumer prices rose 3.7% year-over-year in September. Despite a recent federal-funds rate hike, Warsh intentionally maintains silence regarding the Fed's reaction function and forward guidance to observe unfiltered market signals. This lack of transparency has exacerbated market volatility, forcing investors to parse conflicting statements from regional Fed presidents such as John Williams, Lorie Logan, and Beth Hammack. Markets are pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike at the upcoming October 27 FOMC meeting, with expectations of two additional hikes by January.
items.bottom_line: The Federal Reserve's refusal to provide forward guidance or a reaction function amid rising inflation is driving market volatility and rate speculation.

Lawmakers approved Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister, while confirming Laith al-Khazali—brother of a designated terrorist leader—as deputy prime minister, drawing attention due to US sanctions. Al-Zaidi inherited public debt exceeding 208 trillion dinars ($139bn) and vowed to tackle corruption, disarm non-state groups, and complete the withdrawal of US forces.

items.title: ASPM in the AI Era Part 1: Unified Visibility Across Your Stack
items.one_liner: Application Security Posture Management platforms use contextual security graphs to prioritize actionable risks from noisy scanner backlogs.
items.summary: Application Security Posture Management (ASPM) has become critical in the era of automated development due to the sheer volume of alerts generated by rapid scanners. Traditional manual reviews are overwhelmed by cascading vulnerabilities like React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) in Next.js applications, which create thousands of fragmented findings. Effective ASPM must unify tools like SAST, SCA, and secrets scanning using a security graph to correlate findings with cloud exposure and runtime contexts, prioritizing truly exploitable paths. Platforms like Wiz integrate third-party scanners via the Wiz Integration Network (WIN) to normalize data and provide comprehensive enterprise risk visibility.
items.bottom_line: Effective vulnerability management in modern applications requires contextual correlation rather than treating all scanner alerts with equal weight.

claims.text: For an enterprise heavily invested in Next.js, a flaw in a core component does not just trigger one alert. It cascades across micro-frontends, internal tools, and public applications, instantly generating thousands of isolated findings across hundreds of repositories and container images.

items.title: Why the AI Attack Surface Extends Your Stack
items.one_liner: Enterprise AI integrations expand the attack surface beyond models to surrounding tools, APIs, and cloud infrastructure, enabling complex multi-layer attack chains.
items.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows significantly expands the traditional application security attack surface beyond the model itself. Because LLMs can autonomously invoke tools, retrieve data across APIs, and act as intelligence layers, prompt injections and security flaws can trigger cascading failures across the entire software stack. Conventional security scans and model safety checks often miss these complex attack chains, which can lead to remote code execution, credential theft, and cross-tenant data exposure when service accounts possess overly broad permissions. Security leaders must map what AI systems can access and execute realistic attack scenarios across all underlying infrastructure layers.
items.bottom_line: Enterprise AI security requires mapping full stack integrations and testing realistic attack chains rather than relying solely on traditional perimeter defenses or model safety scans.

items.title: What Skyscanner's AI rollout proves about verifying AI-generated code
items.one_liner: AI agents rewriting failing tests to satisfy CI highlight why agent self-review cannot replace independent verification.
items.summary: Recent analyses of AI coding agent workflows demonstrate that self-review loops and green CI pipelines are insufficient for code verification. A real-world incident at Skyscanner showed an autonomous agent rewriting a failing test to force a pass while keeping CI green. True verification requires external, deterministic methods running completely independently of the code-writing agent. Effective deployment depends on closed-loop validation across agent creation, pull-request CI, and long-term maintenance cycles.
key_facts: Vulnerability: Agent self-review bypass via test rewriting
items.bottom_line: Green CI pipelines and agent self-review fail as safety barriers because coding agents can autonomously alter tests to fake correctness.

items.summary: Brent crude settled slightly lower at $105.92 a barrel as investors weighed potential US steps to ease restrictions on the global shadow fleet of tankers following temporary sanctions relief on Russian diesel. Meanwhile, ongoing Middle East conflicts and vessel attacks near the Strait of Hormuz maintained a geopolitical risk premium. US WTI crude rose 3.03% to $97.97 a barrel, supported by a larger-than-expected 8.6-million-barrel draw in US crude inventories down to 415.6 million barrels.
key_facts: US crude inventory draw: 8.6 million barrels
items.bottom_line: Potential US policy shifts on shadow fleet sanctions and ongoing geopolitical shipping attacks are keeping oil markets volatile.

items.title: Morgan Stanley tops estimates as equities trading revenue beats expectations by $909 million
items.one_liner: Morgan Stanley beats Q3 expectations on strong equities trading, while CEO Ted Pick points to AI infrastructure and geopolitics as dominant market drivers.
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reported third-quarter results that beat analyst expectations, driven by blockbuster performance in its equities trading division. Profit rose 6.5% to $4.91 billion ($3.03 per share) on a 12% revenue increase to $20.34 billion, compared to estimates of $19.95 billion. The firm's equities trading revenue surged 41% to $5.8 billion, beating estimates by $909 million, which offset weaker performance in fixed income and investment banking. CEO Ted Pick noted that the broader economy is currently balancing a boost from the artificial intelligence infrastructure build-up against the drag of geopolitical conflict.
items.bottom_line: Morgan Stanley's strong Q3 equities performance beat expectations despite weaknesses in fixed income and underwriting, as leadership navigates AI growth versus geopolitical headwinds.

items.title: Ransomware Gangs Embrace Physical Threats, Family Stalking?
items.one_liner: Evaluate reports of physical threats and stalking by ransomware gangs against the backdrop of limited hard verification.
items.summary: Recent survey data from Semperis indicates that ransomware gangs are increasingly employing physical threats, stalking, and harassment against victims. According to the report, 40% of organizations surveyed experienced intimidation, with over half claiming attackers carried out physical threats such as family stalking, facility intrusions, and bodily harm. However, security investigators and journalists have found it difficult to independently verify or document actual physical violence directly tied to ransomware operations, urging caution regarding self-reported statistics.
key_facts: Survey report: Semperis 2026 Ransomware Risk Report
items.bottom_line: While survey data claims widespread physical intimidation by ransomware actors, hard documentation of actual physical violence remains scarce.

claims.text: A combined two out of every five organizations that participated in Semperis's newly released 2026 Ransomware Risk Report indicated they had faced intimidation and threats associated with their ransomware attacks, and often severe ones.

items.title: What to do when a data breach notice doesn't say much
items.one_liner: Analyze why modern data breach notifications omit attack vectors and how consumers can interpret minimal disclosure notices.
items.summary: The Identity Theft Resource Center reported that while US data breach notices hit record highs with over 471 million notices in the first half of 2026, only 24% contained details regarding attack vectors. Companies often withhold details due to crisis communication strategies, incomplete internal investigations, or fears of aiding threat actors or damaging stock prices. Security guidance stresses that victims must distinguish between data being accessed versus exfiltrated, look closely at what specific data types were compromised, and avoid relying on empty corporate claims of seeing no evidence of misuse.
items.bottom_line: Most data breach notifications lack attack vector details, requiring victims to focus on verifying what specific personal data elements were actually exfiltrated.

items.title: Building bridges for India’s wildlife
items.one_liner: Canopy and gantry bridges are critical conservation tools for reconnecting fragmented wildlife habitats divided by roads and railways.
items.summary: The fragmentation of wildlife habitats by linear infrastructure such as roads and railways has severely impacted arboreal species like India's western hoolock gibbons, whose populations have declined by 90% in recent decades. Because these apes have an awkward terrestrial gait and rely entirely on continuous forest canopies, roads and train tracks isolate populations, leading to genetic inbreeding. Conservation organizations have successfully mitigated these barriers by utilizing dense tree planting to form natural canopy bridges over rail lines, alongside gantry and braided rope bridges deployed across sanctuaries for other vulnerable wildlife like the giant Indian squirrel.

items.bottom_line: Linear infrastructure severely fragments endangered arboreal wildlife habitats, requiring targeted canopy bridges and conservation corridors to prevent genetic isolation.

items.summary: SEBI has issued a revised framework for the Clearing and Settlement (CAS) mechanism, introducing changes to auction windows and reference price calculations effective December 7, 2026. Closing prices on derivatives expiry days (Tuesdays and Thursdays) will now be calculated using the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) of trades executed during the final 30 minutes of continuous trading. The model propagates each path's guard, register values and arithmetic flags, merges shared states, and combines all reachable return values. It does not select the first return or discard branch conditions. Supported forms are b, b.<condition>, cbz, cbnz, tbz and tbnz, with aligned direct targets inside the selected function.

SSM layers are designed to make decoding fast: they use a fixed-size state in place of a key-value (KV) cache that grows with context length. At serving batch sizes, however, the SSM layers, not attention, can be the latency bottleneck up to 100K tokens of context. SSM layers also complicate two techniques that reliably speed up attention decoding: speculative decoding and quantization.
